verdict.rationale: Rootly documents a REST API with an OpenAPI spec and API keys, plus an official MCP server that exposes incident data and actions to MCP clients such as Claude Code. That supports agent-driven incident creation and generic "take action" calls. However, the pack never shows API or MCP operations for acknowledging, escalating, or resolving incidents; acknowledge/escalate/resolve is only documented inside Microsoft Teams, which is a chat surface. missing for 10: documented API/MCP acknowledge, escalate, and resolve operations, an MCP tool list covering the full incident lifecycle, independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven end-to-end handling.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, my agent can acknowledge, escalate, and resolve incidents end to end through a documented API or MCP connection — no dashboard in the loop

citations.quote: The Rootly MCP Server implements the Model Context Protocol to expose Rootly incident data and actions as tools that any MCP-compatible client can use.
query incidents, check on-call schedules, find similar past incidents, and take action
The Rootly API allows you to create incidents automatically from monitoring tools, CI/CD pipelines, internal services, or any external automation system.
Download the OpenAPI/Swagger specification to explore the Rootly API endpoints or generate client libraries.
